assign.request: UX rethink pass 2 on /imagine/youtube/ (the youtube realm): five sentences, try an alternative layout for real and measure it, make it more visual, check persistence, resolve and land.
steps: fix five sub-lab icons -> real stills
ui-test the primary gesture, check console

log.msg: FIVE SENTENCES (before). what: a page taking the YouTube IFrame Player API apart into six small labs -- a live control panel, a chaptered talk, and three ways a shared timeline can drive other UI. use: click a lab in the left picker (panel is already open), press play on the poster, then drive it with the buttons or the keyboard. goal: understand, by playing with it, everything the API exposes and how a page can react to time passing in a video with no time event. hard: 3/5 -- panel opens by default with a genuinely dense grid of controls, but the other five labs (Course, Yield, Split, Chat, Marks) are one-word names that say nothing until clicked. better: replace the five icons with real stills of what each lab looks like, and split panel's tall single control column into controls-left / player-centre / readouts-right so its 8 stacked blocks stop running one under another.

ALTERNATIVE BUILT: panel/page.js's single yt-controls stack (8 groups, one column) split into a real 3-column card -- seeking/transport/shortcuts left, the video centre, readouts/speed/sound/source/feed right. `.yt-panel { container-type: inline-size }` + `@container (min-width: 56em)` reorders left/centre/right only once the row is actually wide enough for three real columns; below that the DOM's own video-first order stands, so a narrow cold landing still meets the video before the controls (a first attempt used an unconditional css `order` and made the narrow case WORSE -- video pushed below 3 control groups, scrollH 1199 -> 1377px at 1280 -- caught by measuring, reverted to the container-query version).

MEASURED (panel column's own body, not the pinned document): height at 3440: 1110px -> 859px scrollHeight against an 852px viewport box -- the column no longer needs to scroll internally at all. At 1280: 1199px -> 988px. Width used at 3440 (right edge of widest real content / 3440) and dead space are UNCHANGED, 2412px/70.1% used, 1028px dead on the right -- expected and already known (doc/decisions.md 2026-09-04): that band is the columns row holding space for a sibling column, not fixable by this page (widening was tried and reverted twice site-wide). KEPT: shorter page, same width story, same or better legibility (video grew because both side columns are narrower than the old single 34em stack).

VISUAL: /imagine/youtube/'s own picker was a plain icon+one-word list (Control panel, Course, Yield, Split, Chat, Marks) -- core's default column() row list. Set `index: true` on youtube/page.js and called `this.previews()` on a Map excluding `panel` (already open beside it, same reasoning course/'s own index:true uses for its chapter bar) to draw the remaining five as real-still cards instead: added `preview(nav)` to course/yield/split/chat/marks pointing at a real Playwright screenshot of that lab's own distinguishing UI (course's colored chapter bar, yield's video-already-stepped-aside corner shot, split's video+form, chat's video+room, marks' Mark/Clear+output array), saved at public/imagine/youtube/shots/<slug>.jpg, one shared `.yt-shot{object-fit:cover}` css rule. No core edit needed -- previews()/preview_card() already support this (design/color, gallery/cards use the identical pattern).

BUG FOUND AND FIXED: yield/page.js declared a method named `card(title, fn)` for its wizard steps. core's Page.nav() reads `this.card` as a page's SIZE-modifier field (`.two`/`.tall`/`.big`) and preview_card() does `.ac(nav.card)` -- View.ac(arg) calls arg.split(" "), so the method itself (truthy, not a string) threw `arg.split is not a function` the instant yield got a real preview() (2026-09-05, only surfaced because this task gave it one). Renamed to `step_card`, three call sites updated, one-line comment left naming the exact collision (the same class of bug Page.class.js's own `opens()` comment already warns about). Verified: zero console errors at 400/1280/1920/3440 after the fix.

UI-TEST (ui-test skill, drive.mjs): re-verified yesterday's default-column activate()/deactivate() fix survives today's restructuring. Plan A -- cold load /imagine/youtube/ (never routed to /panel/), press key M with zero clicks: .yt-panel .yt-feed-row count 0 -> 1, content ["0:00mute()"] -- the keyboard legend fires on a cold load. Plan B -- click .yt-start (real play), wait 4s: Player.live=1, Player.all.at(-1).state()=1 (playing); click the real breadcrumb link to /imagine/ (in-app SPA nav, not a reload); Player.live reads 0 afterwards -- the poll dies with the page. Both confirmed NOT regressed. pngs copied to shots/uitest-*.png.

PERSISTENCE: grep -rn store()|localStorage across public/imagine/youtube/ -- zero hits outside doc/decisions.md's own record of two ALREADY-OPEN, ALREADY-DEFERRED proposals (marks/ writing its table, split/'s form) that were never implemented. This realm persists nothing. Console: zero errors at 400/1280/1920/3440 throughout.

FIVE SENTENCES (after). what: a page that lets you actually drive the YouTube IFrame Player API -- a live control panel with controls on one side, the video in the middle, and every readout on the other -- plus five more labs proving what a shared, polled timeline can drive. use: press play on the video in the middle, then drive it with the buttons on the left or the keyboard; click a card below to open one of the other five labs, each with a real picture of what it looks like. goal: leave understanding, by playing with it, everything the API exposes and how a page reacts to time passing in a video that has no time event. hard: 2/5 -- the panel now reads left-to-right as drive it / watch it / read it, and the five labs show what they do instead of just naming themselves. better: wire the marks/ cue table in as a live companion column beside panel by default, so the page also shows where its own cue tables come from without a click (flagged, not built -- a real design decision the owner should make, not a caveat-and-ship fix, per doc/decisions.md's 2026-09-04 entry).

assign.outcome: **Built and kept the 3-column card on `/imagine/youtube/panel/`** — seeking/transport/keyboard-legend left, the video centre, readouts+speed+sound+source+feed right, reordering itself with a `@container` query (not a fixed `order`, which a first attempt showed makes a narrow cold landing worse). Measured: the panel column's own scrollHeight at 3440 went 1110px -> 859px (fits its 852px box, no internal scroll left); at 1280, 1199px -> 988px. Width used/dead space at 3440 unchanged (2412px/70.1%/1028px) — that band is the columns row's, not this page's, per 2026-09-04's own record. Replaced the top-level page's plain icon+one-word picker (Course/Yield/Split/Chat/Marks) with real-still preview cards, one screenshot per lab's own distinguishing UI. Found and fixed a real bug the new preview() surfaced: `yield/page.js` had a method named `card()` that shadowed core's `nav().card` field and crashed `preview_card()` — renamed to `step_card`. Re-verified with `ui-test` that yesterday's default-column activate()/deactivate() fix still holds: the keyboard legend fires on a cold load (zero clicks, M -> mute() logged) and `Player.live` drops back to 0 after navigating away mid-play. Persistence: none. Zero console errors at 400/1280/1920/3440. PROPOSED (0) — everything fit inside this module's own fence.
